sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Indian River Systems** (भारतीय नदी प्रणाली) divided primarily into **Himalayan Rivers** and **Peninsular Rivers**.
Evolution traced back to the **Tertiary Period** (Himalayan) and **Gondwana Landmass stability** (Peninsular).
Spans across the entire **Indian Subcontinent**, flowing into the **Bay of Bengal** and the **Arabian Sea**.
Studied under **Physical Geography** and **Drainage Systems** for **UPSSSC PET** candidates.
Crucial for **agriculture**, **hydroelectric power**, **irrigation**, and forms the core of **UPSSSC PET Geography questions**.
**Perennial nature** of Himalayan rivers vs. **seasonal flow** of Peninsular rivers; major **deltas** and **estuaries**.
**Ganga River Basin**, **Indus Basin**, **Brahmaputra Basin**, **Godavari Basin**, and **Krishna Basin**.
Includes **dendritic**, **trellis**, **rectangular**, and **radial** drainage patterns across different terrains.

items.title: 1. Himalayan River Systems (**Ganga, Brahmaputra & Indus**)
items.content:
• Origin: **Glaciers** in the **Great Himalayas**.
• Flow: **Perennial** rivers fed by melting snow and monsoon rains.
• Valleys: Deep **gorges**, **V-shaped valleys**, rapids, and waterfalls in upper reaches.
• Plains: **Meanders**, oxbow lakes, and vast **alluvial plains** in middle and lower courses.
• **Mnemonic:** **'GIB'** -> **G**anga, **I**ndus, **B**rahmaputra are the **Big Three Himalayan Rivers**.

items.title: 2. Peninsular River Systems (**Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Narmada & Tapti**)
items.content:
• Origin: **Western Ghats** and **Central Highlands**.
• Flow: **Seasonal (Non-perennial)** dependent entirely on monsoon rainfall.
• Valleys: Broad, shallow, and mature **graded valleys**.
• Flow Direction: Most flow east into the **Bay of Bengal**; **Narmada and Tapti** flow west into the **Arabian Sea** through rift valleys.
• **Mnemonic:** **'MAA Baap GEte'** -> West-flowing major rivers: **M**ahi, **A**ravalli/Amarkantak (**Narmada**), **T**apti, **G**o (Gujarat).

items.title: 3. Ganga River System & UP Significance
items.content:
• Origin: **Gangotri Glacier** (as **Bhagirathi**) meeting **Alaknanda** at **Devprayag**.
• Total Length: **2,525 km** (Longest river in India).
• UP Flow: Enters UP at **Bijnor** district and exits near **Ballia**; maximum length is in Uttar Pradesh.
• Left Bank Tributaries: **Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi**.
• Right Bank Tributaries: **Yamuna, Son, Punpun**.
• **Mnemonic:** **'Ram Goes Greater Gradually Kept Yamuna Safe'** -> **R**amganga, **G**omti, **G**haghara, **G**andak, **K**osi, **Y**amuna, **S**on.

items.title: 4. Yamuna River System & Major Tributaries
items.content:
• Origin: **Yamunotri Glacier** at the Bandarpoonch peak in the Himalayas.
• Length: **1,376 km** (Longest tributary of Ganga).
• Confluence: Meets Ganga at **Prayagraj** (Triveni Sangam).
• Right Bank Tributaries: **Chambal, Betwa, Ken** (Originating from Peninsular India).
• Left Bank Tributaries: **Tons, Hindon, Rind**.
• **Mnemonic:** **'CBK'** -> **C**hambal, **B**etwa, **K**en (Famous right-bank tributaries of Yamuna).

items.title: 5. Brahmaputra & Indus River Systems
items.content:
• Brahmaputra Origin: **Chemaungdung Glacier** near Lake Mansarovar (known as **Tsangpo** in Tibet, **Dihang** in Arunachal, **Brahmaputra** in Assam, **Jamuna** in Bangladesh).
• Indus Origin: **Mansarovar Lake** (Tibetan Plateau); flows through Ladakh into Pakistan.
• Indus Tributaries: **Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** (The Panjnad rivers).
• **Mnemonic:** **'JCRBS'** -> **J**helum, **C**henab, **R**avi, **B**eas, **S**utlej (North to South order in Punjab plain).

items.definition: Remember the order of confluences on Alaknanda using **'V-N-K-R-D'**: **V**ishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), **N**andaprayag (Nandakini), **K**arnaprayag (Pindar), **R**udraprayag (Mandakini), **D**evprayag (Bhagirathi).

items.term: Trick 2: West Flowing Rivers of Peninsular India
items.definition: Use the acronym **'SMART'**: **S**abarmati, **M**ahi, **A**rmo (Narmada), **R**ao (Tapi - wait, **N**armada, **T**apti, **M**ahi, **S**abarmati).

items.term: Trick 3: Left Bank Tributaries of Ganga (West to East)
items.definition: Use the phrase **'Ram Goes Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi'**: **R**amganga, **G**omti, **G**haghara, **G**andak, **K**osi.
Use the mnemonic **'J-C-R-B-S'**: **J**helum, **C**henab, **R**avi, **B**eas, **S**utlej.

items.term: Trick 5: Rivers forming Estuaries instead of Deltas
items.definition: Remember **'NaMo TaBa'**: **Na**rmada, **Mo**hi (Mahi - partial), **Ta**pti, **Ba**ran (Focus on **Narmada and Tapti** as major estuary formers).

items.term: Trick 6: Brahmaputra Names in Different Regions
items.definition: Remember **'T-D-B-J'**: **T**sangpo (Tibet), **D**ihang (Arunachal), **B**rahmaputra (Assam), **J**amuna (Bangladesh).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Yamuna and Brahmaputra Lengths
items.definition: Students often confuse Yamuna's length (**1,376 km**) with Narmada's length (**1,312 km**). Brahmaputra is total **2,900 km** but only **916 km** inside India.

items.term: Mistake 2: Flow Direction of Narmada & Tapti
items.definition: Remember that **Narmada and Tapti** flow **West** into the Arabian Sea, unlike most major peninsular rivers that flow **East** into the Bay of Bengal.
Ganga does not originate as 'Ganga' directly; it is formed by the confluence of **Bhagirathi and Alaknanda** at **Devprayag**.

items.term: Mistake 4: Longest River in India vs. South India
items.definition: **Ganga** is the longest river **in India** (2,525 km), while **Godavari** is the longest river in **Peninsular India** (Dakshin Ganga).
The **Son River** is a **right-bank tributary of Ganga** that flows **Northwards** from Amarkantak, not Southwards.
Divided into **Himalayan Drainage** (perennial, antecedent) and **Peninsular Drainage** (seasonal, superimposed).
Largest river basin in India covering 11 states, with the maximum catchment area in **Uttar Pradesh**.
Governs water sharing of Indus rivers; India controls **Beas, Ravi, Sutlej**; Pakistan controls **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab**.
Known for heavy siltation, shifting river channels, and massive annual floods in **Assam**.
Referred to as **'Dakshin Ganga'** or **'Vridha Ganga'** due to its large size and basin area among peninsular rivers.
Flows through a rift valley between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges.
World's largest and fastest-growing delta formed by the **Ganga and Brahmaputra** rivers before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
Located on the **Brahmaputra River** in Assam; recognized as the world's largest river island.
Famous for extensive **ravine erosion** (Badland topography) in the Chambal river valley across MP, Rajasthan, and UP.
Key rivers flowing through UP include **Ganga, Yamuna, Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Rapti, and Betwa**.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on the tributaries of Ganga (specifically Gomti, Ghaghara, and Yamuna) and river-bank cities like Varanasi, Kanpur, Ayodhya, and Gorakhpur.
Memorize the exact lengths of Ganga (2,525 km) and Yamuna (1,376 km) as direct factual questions frequently appear in the PET exam.
Examiners often trap students by asking whether Narmada flows into the Bay of Bengal. Always remember Narmada and Tapti flow West into the Arabian Sea.
Do not confuse 'Dakshin Ganga' (Godavari) with 'Cauvery', which is sometimes called the 'Ganga of the South' based on religious sanctity.

keyTakeaways: Ganga is India's longest river (2,525 km), originating from Gangotri and ending in the Sundarban Delta.
Peninsular rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri flow east into the Bay of Bengal, forming fertile deltas.
Narmada and Tapti flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries instead of deltas.
Yamuna is Ganga's longest tributary, meeting it at Prayagraj with major peninsular right-bank tributaries like Chambal, Betwa, and Ken.
Panch Prayag represents the sacred confluences of Alaknanda with other Himalayan rivers in Uttarakhand.
Brahmaputra originates near Mansarovar, flows as Tsangpo, Dihang, Brahmaputra, and Jamuna, and hosts Majuli river island.
